title.en: Verghese Kurien: I Too Had a Dream (a letter)

text.en: A grandfather writes a letter to his grandson Siddharth. He tells him why writing letters is better than a quick phone call, and what his own dream was.

The text is a letter written in Anand in 2005 by Dr Verghese Kurien to his grandson Siddharth, beginning with 'My dear Siddharth'.
He says that in today's fast-paced world people prefer the telephone, but a phone call gives only fleeting joy, while writing lasts.
He could have become the head of a big company, an Army general or a successful NRI in the US.
But he chose to work in Anand, Gujarat, because he felt he could make a more meaningful contribution there.
He remembers the ceremony in Delhi in 1999 where the President gave him the Padma Vibhushan and Siddharth put the medal around his neck.
He explains that the medal belongs to the farmers who made the milk cooperative possible, and does not belong to one person.
Dr Kurien is known as the father of India's White Revolution, which made India a leading milk producer.
A letter has a format: address, date, salutation, body, closing and signature.
The message is to follow a dream that serves others, and to give credit to the people who share in the success.
Words: addicted means dependent on something, and fleeting means lasting a very short time.
